exposure: Delivery mode (elective cesarean section, emergency cesarean section, operative vaginal delivery, unassisted vaginal delivery)
outcome: Maternal transfer to intensive care units
cohort: The study included 169,583 low-risk primiparous women with singleton, cephalic labors at >= 37 weeks who delivered in Norway between 1999 and 2009.
finding: Most adverse outcomes and operative deliveries increased with increasing maternal age, although the increase in absolute risks was generally low.
mod_finding: Moderate blood loss was three times more likely in elective and emergency cesarean sections than in unassisted vaginal delivery, and while emergency operative procedures increased risk, the absolute risk difference in complications between different modes of delivery was low for most outcomes.
